methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $33M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
Molten Industries is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by Caleb Boyd and Kevin Bush, having raised $32.9M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable set of 9 private and 1 public company in the sector, including peer-stage reference points such as Generalist AI ($2.0B Series B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B Series B), and Walden Robotics ($1.1B Seed).

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $32.9M raised as a proxy for post-money value and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-round progression, yielding $66M. Peer-median analysis benchmarks against the four comparable companies listed above, producing a median valuation of $1.7B with a range of $1.1B to $2.0B.

The triangulated analysis across both methods supports a valuation range of $56M to $2.0B, with a median of $883M. The wide spread reflects material uncertainty regarding Molten's competitive positioning relative to more mature Series B cohort peers. The peer-median approach is anchored to later-stage comparables (predominantly Series B), which likely overstates fair value for a current Series A company absent material evidence of accelerated milestone achievement. Stage-progression offers a conservative floor but depends on assumed forward execution. Reconciliation toward the $100M–$300M range may be warranted pending visibility into product-market fit metrics and near-term revenue trajectory.
